copy.en:
How did Earth's features form?

Charles Lyell's uniformitarianism principle says the same slow processes we see today — like erosion and sedimentation — shaped Earth over very long spans of time!
copy.tl:
Paano nabuo ang mga features ng Earth?

Sabi ng uniformitarianism principle ni Charles Lyell, ang parehong mabagal na proseso ngayon — gaya ng erosion at sedimentation — ang nagbago sa Earth sa napakahabang panahon!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagporma sa mga features sa Yuta?

Sa prinsipyong uniformitarianism ni Charles Lyell, ang mao ra nga hinay nga proseso karon — sama sa erosion ug sedimentation — ang nag-usab sa Yuta sulod sa taas kaayo nga panahon!

Parang ensayo! May patay o mahinang bahagi ng germ ang bakuna na hindi nagpapasakit, pero sapat para matuto ang katawan gumawa ng depensang handa sa totoong sakit.

Is a giraffe bigger than an elephant?

Not really! The giraffe is taller, but the elephant is LARGER—because size means how heavy and wide the whole body is, not just height.
copy.tl:
Mas malaki ba ang giraffe kaysa elepante?

Hindi pala! Mas mataas ang giraffe, pero mas MALAKI ang elepante—dahil ang laki ay tungkol sa kabigatan at kalapad ng buong katawan, hindi lang sa taas.

Rolling resistance is the friction force between a tire and the road! Underinflated tires have higher rolling resistance, causing greater fuel consumption.

Ang rolling resistance ay ang puwersa ng kiskisan ng gulong sa daan! Ang mga gulong na kulang sa hangin ay may mas malaking rolling resistance, kaya mas mabilis maubusan ng gasolina.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang rolling resistance, ug nganong mas daghang gasolina ang gulong nga kulang sa hangin?

Ang rolling resistance mao ang kiskisan sa gulong ug daan! Ang gulong nga kulang sa hangin adunay mas taas nga rolling resistance, nagdugang sa gasolina.

Naa sa ilalom sa iyang tunok, dili sa unod! Parehas usab sa stonefish — didto gitago ang ilang hilo.

assignedReviews.reason: The card states a structural fact about the skeletal system (33 vertebrae) but does not describe how the skeletal system works, which is the focus of G4-L-1. It shares the skeletal-system topic but provides no functional explanation.

copy.en: A child's backbone isn't just one bone—it's made of 33 small bones stacked together called vertebrae.
copy.tl: Ang gulugod ng isang bata ay hindi iisang buto lang—33 na maliliit na buto na tinatawag na vertebrae ang bumubuo nito.
copy.bis: Ang gulugod sa usa ka bata dili usa lang ka bukog—33 ka gagmay nga bukog nga gitawag og vertebrae ang naghimo niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: your immune system fights back with antibodies
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the immune system's response to dengue virus, but the competency requires using models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations to explain how body systems work together (e.g., digestion and excretion). The card uses none of these representations and does not address the coordinated functioning of body systems as specified.

copy.en:
How does the body fight dengue?

When dengue virus invades, your immune system fights back with antibodies that attack like soldiers. Fever is a sign of that battle, and slowly you recover.
copy.tl:
Paano nakikipaglaban ang katawan sa dengue?

Kapag pumasok ang dengue virus, lumalaban ang immune system gamit ang antibodies na parang mga sundalong sumasalakay dito. Ang lagnat ay senyales ng labanang ito, at unti-unti kang gumaling.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagpakig-away sa lawas sa dengue?

Kon mosulod ang dengue virus, makig-away ang imong immune system pinaagi sa antibodies nga murag mga sundalo nga moataki niini. Ang hilanat maoy timailhan sa maong gubat, ug hinay-hinay ka nga mag-ayo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the virus makes throat muscles spasm painfully
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a specific rabies symptom (throat muscle spasms causing hydrophobia) but does not describe how the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, or respiratory systems work. It only mentions muscles in passing, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Why do rabies patients fear water?

Rabies can cause a strange fear of water — the virus makes throat muscles spasm painfully, so swallowing becomes terrifying.
copy.tl:
Bakit natatakot sa tubig ang may rabies?

Isang kakaibang sintomas ng rabies ay matinding takot sa tubig — dahil pinipigil ng virus ang kalamnan sa lalamunan, kaya sobrang sakit lumunok.
copy.bis:
Nganong mahadlok sa tubig ang naay rabies?

Usa ka katingad-an nga sintomas sa rabies mao ang grabeng kahadlok sa tubig — kay ang bayrus mohigot sa unod sa tutunlan, mao nga sakit kaayo motulon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Many viruses travel in tiny droplets of spit that fly out when a sick person coughs or sneezes.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions coughing and sneezing, which are respiratory actions, but it does not identify the parts of the respiratory system (nose, windpipe, lungs) or describe how they work. It only describes virus transmission, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Many viruses travel in tiny droplets of spit that fly out when a sick person coughs or sneezes.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes how viruses spread from a sick person to others, which is an interaction between living things that can cause harm. However, it does not explain the interaction or its good/harm effects in the context of the competency; it merely states a transmission mechanism. It is related to the topic but does not directly teach the competency.

copy.en: Many viruses travel in tiny droplets of spit that fly out when a sick person coughs or sneezes.
copy.tl: Maraming virus ang kumakalat sa maliliit na patak ng laway na lumalabas kapag umuubo o bumabahing ang taong may sakit.
copy.bis: Daghang bayrus mokaylap sa gagmay nga tulo sa laway nga molupad kon mag-ubo o mobahin ang tawong masakiton.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: dark gray to black hair all over its body
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the pig's coat color, which is an outer body part, but it does not describe the named parts (head, legs, wings) or their roles in movement and food gathering. It only mentions hair color, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: dark gray to black hair all over its body
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a single animal's coat color and does not use a table or classify living things into the named groups. It provides no classification information, so it does not support the competency.

copy.en: The Visayan warty pig wears a natural coat of dark gray to black hair all over its body.
copy.tl: May likas na balahibong maitim hanggang abuhin ang buong katawan ng Visayan warty pig.
copy.bis: Adunay natural nga balhibo nga itom ngadto sa abohon ang tibuok lawas sa Visayan warty pig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The higher the viscosity, the slower the flow speed!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses viscosity and flow speed, which is a property of liquids but not the shape/volume properties (definite/indefinite shape and volume) that G5-M-3 requires. It shares the topic of liquid properties but does not directly support describing solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume.

copy.en:
How does viscosity affect a liquid's flow speed?

The higher the viscosity, the slower the flow speed!
copy.tl:
Paano nakakaapekto ang viscosity sa bilis ng pagdaloy ng likido?

Habang mas mataas ang viscosity, mas mabagal ang takbo ng pagdaloy!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pag-apekto ang viscosity sa katulin sa pagdagayday sa likido?

Kung mas taas ang viscosity, mas hinay ang katulin sa pagdagayday!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It measures how thick a liquid is.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses viscosity, a property of liquids, but does not address shape or volume, which are the specific properties required by G5-M-3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Honey has high viscosity and flows slowly
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe that particles are constantly in motion, have spaces between them, attract each other, and move faster as the temperature increases (or with the addition of heat)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes macroscopic flow behavior but does not mention particles, their motion, spacing, attraction, or temperature effects, which are the focus of G7-M-3.

copy.en:
Ever wonder why honey pours so slowly compared to water?

That's viscosity! It measures how thick a liquid is. Honey has high viscosity and flows slowly, while water has low viscosity and flows quickly.
copy.tl:
Napapaisip ka ba kung bakit mas mabagal bumubuhos ang pulot kaysa tubig?

Iyan ang viscosity! Sukat ito ng kapal ng likido. Mataas ang viscosity ng pulot kaya mabagal dumaloy, pero mababa ang sa tubig kaya mabilis ito.
copy.bis:
Natingala ka ba ngano mas mabagal magbubo ang dugos kaysa sa tubig?

Mao na ang viscosity! Sukod kini sa kapal sa likido. Taas ang viscosity sa dugos mao nga mabagal moagos, pero ubos ang sa tubig mao nga paspas.

copy.en:
What happens if you lack vitamin A?

Not getting enough vitamin A can cause trouble seeing in the dark, so it's important to eat sweet potato and squash.
copy.tl:
Ano ang mangyayari kung kulang sa bitamina A?

Ang kakulangan sa bitamina A ay maaaring magdulot ng hirap makakita sa dilim, kaya mahalagang kumain ng kamote at kalabasa.
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo kon kulang sa bitamina A?

Ang kakulang sa bitamina A mahimong hinungdan sa kalisod makakita sa kangitngit, busa importante mokaon og kamote ug kalabasa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Carrots, sweet potato, and malunggay are packed with vitamin A
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a specific nutrient (vitamin A) and its benefit to eyesight, not the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter). It mentions food only as a source of vitamin A, not as a basic need, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Carrots, sweet potato, and malunggay are packed with vitamin A, which helps keep your eyesight clear and your eyes healthy.
copy.tl: Puno ng vitamin A ang karot, kamote, at malunggay, na tumutulong manatiling malinaw at malusog ang paningin mo.
copy.bis: Puno sa vitamin A ang karot, kamote, ug malunggay, nga nagatabang aron magpabilin nga klaro ug himsog ang imong panan-aw.

copy.en: Calamansi, oranges, and guava are full of vitamin C — it helps your body fight illness and heal wounds faster.
copy.tl: Puno ng bitamina C ang kalamansi, dalandan, at bayabas — tumutulong ito labanan ang sakit at mapabilis ang paggaling ng sugat.
copy.bis: Puno sa bitamina C ang kalamansi, kahel, ug bayabas — makatabang kini makigbatok sa sakit ug mopadali sa pag-ayo sa samad.

copy.en: Vitamin C and the B vitamins are water-soluble, meaning they dissolve in water.
copy.tl: Ang Vitamin C at ang mga Vitamin B ay water-soluble, ibig sabihin natutunaw ang mga ito sa tubig.
copy.bis: Ang Vitamin C ug ang mga Vitamin B water-soluble, buot ipasabot matunaw kini sa tubig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Without enough Vitamin D, a person can get rickets — a disease that weakens bones and makes them bend.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a disease (rickets) caused by vitamin D deficiency that affects bones, but it does not describe how the skeletal system (or any other body system) works. It provides a fact about bone health rather than instruction on system function, so it is only topically related to the skeletal system component of G4-L-1.

copy.en:
What happens if you lack Vitamin D?

Without enough Vitamin D, a person can get rickets — a disease that weakens bones and makes them bend.
copy.tl:
Ano ang mangyayari kung kulang sa Vitamin D?

Kapag kulang sa Vitamin D, maaaring magkaroon ng rickets — sakit na nagpapahina at nagpapabaluktot sa mga buto.
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo kon kulang sa Vitamin D?

Kon kulang sa Vitamin D, mahimong maangkon ang rickets — sakit nga makaluya ug makabaliko sa mga bukog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Vitamin D helps your body use calcium, making teeth stronger and less likely to decay.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses vitamin D's effect on teeth strength via calcium, which is tangentially related to the skeletal system (teeth are part of it), but it does not describe how the skeletal system works (e.g., support, movement, protection, or the roles of bones and joints). It provides no direct instructional support for the competency's action of describing how the body system functions.

copy.en:
Does vitamin D help more than just bones?

Yes—your teeth too! Vitamin D helps your body use calcium, making teeth stronger and less likely to decay.
copy.tl:
May tinutulungan pa ba ang vitamin D bukod sa buto?

Oo—pati ngipin! Tinutulungan ng vitamin D ang katawan na gamitin ang calcium, kaya mas matibay ang ngipin at hindi madaling masira.
copy.bis:
Aduna pa bay laing tabangan ang vitamin D gawas sa bukog?

Oo—apil ang ngipon! Motabang ang vitamin D sa lawas nga magamit ang calcium, mao nga mas lig-on ang ngipon ug dili dali madaot.

copy.en: Not all vitamins come from fruits and veggies — vitamin B12, for example, comes mostly from meat, fish, eggs, and milk.
copy.tl: Hindi lahat ng bitamina ay galing sa gulay at prutas — ang vitamin B12 halimbawa ay madalas galing sa karne, isda, itlog, at gatas.
copy.bis: Dili tanang bitamina gikan sa utanon ug prutas — ang vitamin B12 pananglitan kasagarang gikan sa karne, isda, itlog, ug gatas.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: Vitamin K diet is not the five body systems as a set.

copy.en: Vitamin K, found in leafy greens like kangkong and malunggay, helps your blood clot when you get a cut — stopping the bleeding.
copy.tl: Ang vitamin K na nasa madahong gulay tulad ng kangkong at malunggay ay tumutulong mamuo ang dugo kapag nasugatan ka — para tumigil ang pagdurugo.
copy.bis: Ang vitamin K nga naa sa dahonon nga utanon sama sa kangkong ug malunggay motabang aron mamuo ang dugo kon masamdan ka — aron mohunong ang dugo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: including the ones that release energy from food
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions enzymes speeding up reactions that release energy from food, which touches on respiration, but it does not describe the process of photosynthesis or respiration, nor identify raw materials and products. It is only tangentially related to the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Many vitamins work as partners to enzymes, which speed up reactions
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses vitamins and enzymes in general, but does not describe how any of the listed human body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) work. The mention of energy release from food is too vague to directly support the digestive or respiratory system descriptions.

copy.en: Many vitamins work as partners to enzymes, which speed up reactions — including the ones that release energy from food. So vitamins help with energy, but they aren't the energy itself.
copy.tl: Maraming bitamina ang nagsisilbing katuwang ng mga enzyme, na nagpapabilis ng mga reaksyon — kasama ang paglabas ng enerhiya mula sa pagkain. Kaya tumutulong ang bitamina sa enerhiya, pero hindi ito mismo ang enerhiya.
copy.bis: Daghang bitamina ang nagsilbing katabang sa mga enzyme, nga nagpaspas sa mga reaksyon — lakip na ang pagpagawas og kusog gikan sa pagkaon. Mao nga ang bitamina motabang sa kusog, apan dili kini mismo ang kusog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: we still need them for healthy eyes, bones, and skin, and to keep us from getting sick
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses vitamins as needed for health, but the competency is about identifying basic needs of living things such as air, food, water, and shelter. Vitamins are not one of the listed basic needs, and the card does not teach the concept of basic needs. It shares the broad topic of nutrition but provides no direct instructional support for identifying basic needs.

copy.en:
Do we still need vitamins even without energy?

Yes! Even though vitamins don't give energy, we still need them for healthy eyes, bones, and skin, and to keep us from getting sick.
copy.tl:
Kailangan pa ba ang bitamina kahit walang enerhiya?

Oo! Kahit hindi nagbibigay ng enerhiya ang bitamina, kailangan pa rin natin ito para sa malusog na mata, buto, at balat, at para hindi tayo magkasakit.
copy.bis:
Gikinahanglan pa ba ang bitamina bisan walay enerhiya?

Oo! Bisan dili maghatag og kusog ang bitamina, gikinahanglan gihapon nato kini para sa himsog nga mata, bukog, ug panit, ug aron dili ta magsakit.

It only provides background on the alert level itself.

copy.en: At Alert Level 2, earthquakes and signs increase, meaning magma might be moving upward! The volcano's unrest is rising, so scientists watch it more closely.
copy.tl: Sa Alert Level 2, dumadami ang lindol at senyales na maaaring gumagalaw ang magma paitaas! Tumataas ang pagkabalisa ng bulkan, kaya higit na binabantayan ito ng mga siyentipiko.
copy.bis: Sa Alert Level 2, modaghan ang linog ug timailhan nga tingali ang magma nagsaka! Nagkataas ang pagkabalaka sa bulkan, busa mas suod kini nga bantayan sa mga siyentipiko.

copy.en: Meet the crater! It’s the bowl-shaped opening at the top of a volcano where lava and smoke come out.
copy.tl: Kilalanin ang crater! Ito ang hugis-mangkok na butas sa tuktok ng bulkan kung saan lumalabas ang lava at usok.
copy.bis: Ilha ang crater! Kini ang porma-mangkok nga buho sa tumoy sa bulkan diin mogawas ang lava ug aso.
